perspective:
**Harold Padilla’s available information:**

- Harold knows he is a project manager. He knows Arthur Begum as a friend/police officer whom he relies on for advice and support.
- **Scenario 1:** Harold feels frustrated and anxious about his project’s progress and believes his team is unmotivated. He arranges and attends a coffee-shop meeting with Arthur. Harold tells Arthur the team seems unmotivated and that he is at his wit’s end. He hears Arthur ask whether he has tried understanding each team member’s individual drives; Harold admits he has focused on goals/deadlines. Arthur advises one-on-one conversations and making people feel valued/understood personally. Harold says he will try and feels more hopeful.
- **Scenario 2:** After the talk, Harold feels hopeful and relieved, believes Arthur’s advice will help, and decides to implement it. He tells the team he wants quick one-on-one chats to understand what motivates each of them. Team Member 1 says that could be helpful; Team Member 2 says they are open to it. Harold says he will schedule time with each and asks them to make the project a success together.
- **Scenario 3:** Harold implements the advice but observes/perceives that the team still is not responding well. He feels disappointed and worried. He tells Arthur he tried the suggestions but the team still isn’t responding well. Arthur says there may be deeper issues such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and suggests digging deeper. Harold decides to set up another round of meetings.
- **Scenario 4:** Harold believes there may be underlying team issues he hasn’t addressed. He holds one-on-one meetings and asks team members to share concerns. Team Member 1 tells him there is tension between a few people affecting work. Team Member 2 tells him they feel overwhelmed by the workload and stressed, making motivation hard. Harold says he will look into resolving conflicts and consider redistributing tasks, and tells Team Member 2 their well-being is important.
- **Scenario 5:** Harold feels optimistic and empowered, believing that addressing individual concerns will improve performance. He tells the team he will create a more supportive, open environment through regular feedback sessions and team-building activities. Team Member 1 says that sounds great and will help; Team Member 2 agrees and says it is good their concerns are being addressed. Harold says their input and well-being are crucial and urges them to work together for project success.

Harold has no access to private/internal thoughts of Arthur or the team members beyond what they said or did in his presence, and no access to narrator-only information.
